qtimetadatafield.fieldentry: Hackles College Edition question bank (150 items)

material.mattext: Which set of four features does Module 1 say shows up across the seven risk families?
Passwords, updates, backups and filters
Speed, volume, cost and location
Strangers, screens, games and money
Pressure, secrecy, a request, and a move somewhere more private

Answer D. The kit teaches the pattern, not the app. Pressure, secrecy, a request and a move somewhere more private recur whether the setting is a game, a chat or a feed. Source: Academy Module 1, Part 1 (The thread that connects them)
What is the Hackles routine?
Hackles up? Pause. Check. Tell.
Look. Listen. Learn.
Block. Delete. Forget.
Stop. Drop. Roll.
Answer A. Notice the feeling, do nothing yet, check whether it is real and who is asking, then tell a trusted adult. Source: Academy Overview; Module 1, Part 4
Why does Module 1 say the old 'stranger danger' slogan is not enough online?
Strangers are never a danger to children online
Only adults who are strangers can cause online harm
Much online harm starts with accounts that look like peers or people a child half-knows, so children need to notice pressure, secrecy and requests whoever is asking
Children cannot tell who is a stranger, so they should avoid all online contact
Answer C. The skill taught is noticing the pattern and telling. The slogan misses accounts that seem friendly and familiar. Source: Academy Module 1, 'A word about stranger danger'
Which figure did Module 1 report for NCMEC's 2025 count of financially motivated sextortion reports?
More than 500,000, up from more than 360,000
More than 5,000, up from more than 3,600
About 80,000, a rise of 37 percent
More than 50,000, up from more than 36,000 the year before

Answer D. These are the counts verified on NCMEC's own page. The 80,000 and 37 percent figures could not be found on the primary pages and were removed from the kit. Source: Academy Module 1, Calm Fact 2; Fact-Check Report Round 1, items 4.1 to 4.4
A colleague drafting a newsletter wants to write 'sextortion reports rose 37 percent.' What is the best advice?
Give the counts from NCMEC's page (more than 50,000 in 2025, more than 36,000 in 2024) and avoid a percentage the primary pages do not state
Keep 37 percent because several news sites use it
Round the rise up to 40 percent so it has impact
Drop all numbers and say reports are 'exploding'

Answer A. The kit's check found the 37 percent figure only in snippets, and the counts imply about 39 percent. Quote the counts from the primary source. Source: Evidence file, Section 2.1; Fact-Check Report Round 1, item 4.2
Why does Module 1 call children not telling 'the most important number for teachers'?
It shows that lessons are unnecessary
It proves that children cannot be trusted to report
It shows that most children are being harmed
It shows the most powerful thing to teach is that telling is safe, never gets you in trouble, and brings help
Answer D. The point is help-seeking. Shame and fear of blame keep children silent, so the lesson design aims at telling. Source: Academy Module 1, Calm Fact 4
A candidate wants to quote 'one-third of children told no one and only 3 percent went to police or a helpline.' Which handling is best?
Say the figures come from UNICEF's first 13 countries (Africa and Southeast Asia), not the US, and confirm them in the primary reports before quoting [VERIFY]
Present them as US figures because the topic is the same
Quote them as exact and universal
Add that 97 percent of US children tell a parent

Answer A. Module 1 states the geographic limit. The Round 1 report could not confirm the figures on the project page, so they stay marked for checking. Source: Academy Module 1, Calm Fact 4; Fact-Check Report Round 1, item 4.11
What does the Finkelhor and colleagues (2021) review, as summarized in Module 1, suggest about lesson types?
One large assembly is the best-supported approach
Lectures on rules outperform role-play
Active, skill-based, repeated programs are better supported than one-off assemblies or information-only lessons
Fear-based warnings are proven to work best
Answer C. The summary table in Module 1 favors active, structured, repeated programs. The kit marks the citation [VERIFY] until read in full. Source: Academy Module 1, 'What the research says works'
Which statement is an honest caveat about the evidence for Hackles-style teaching?
A large randomized trial proves the program prevents sextortion
Every claim in the kit has been independently verified
Much of the best evidence comes from an adjacent field, and no rigorous trial of a modern K-12 sextortion or deepfake curriculum is known
Evidence for fear appeals in online safety is conclusive
Answer C. Module 1 and the Assessment Pack both say plainly that no rigorous trial is known and that adjacent-field evidence is used. Source: Academy Module 1; Assessment Pack Section 13
Your principal says, 'One big assembly and we are done for the year.' Which reply fits Module 1?
Refuse and explain that assemblies are harmful
Affirm the goal, then offer both/and: a short kickoff plus ten short classroom lessons, and offer to pilot with one grade
Tell the principal the evidence proves assemblies never work
Agree, since any program is better than none
Answer B. Both/and keeps the visible response the principal wants and adds repeated skill practice. Overstating the evidence would not be honest. Source: Academy Module 1, Scenario 1.A
A fourth grader says, 'I play every night with a guy named Max. He's 14. He gave me free coins.' What is the best first response?
Stay calm and curious ('Tell me more about the game'), do not interrogate, make a quiet note and let the counselor know per school process
Ask the child to show you the whole chat on their device
Ignore it, because it is just a game
'That is dangerous! Never talk to him again!'

Answer A. One comment alone is not a disclosure of harm. Gifts, an older 'friend' and nightly contact are a pattern worth noting. Alarm or interrogation ends the conversation. Source: Academy Module 1, Scenario 1.B
In the Max scenario, which added detail would change your response to treating it as a possible disclosure?
The child says other students also have game friends
The child says Max asked for secrecy, pictures, or a move to a private app, or made threats
The child says Max is good at the game
The child says the coins were colorful

Answer B. Secrecy, pictures, threats or a move to a private app are the signals the kit says to treat as a potential disclosure and handle with the First 10 Minutes. Source: Academy Module 1, Scenario 1.B guidance
Which of these is NOT part of a teacher's role in Hackles?
Reporting as required
Noticing and listening
Handing off to trained people
Investigating who did it and confronting a suspect
Answer D. The role is recognition and response. Investigation, confrontation, viewing images, searching phones and counseling are not the teacher's job. Source: Academy Module 1, Part 5
Why does Module 1 say 'fear without a skill is just fear'?
A child told only that dangers exist has nothing to do with that information, while a rehearsed skill gives them an action
Skills make fear unnecessary for adults
Children cannot feel fear about technology
Fear is never present in children
Answer A. The first reason in 'Why not just scare them' is that fear needs a doable action attached to it. Source: Academy Module 1, Part 3
Module 1 Calm Fact 1 says most children use technology safely most of the time. What follows for teaching?
Build skills calmly for the minority of moments that go wrong, rather than skipping lessons or using scare tactics
Assume every child is already being harmed
Skip online safety lessons
Teach with graphic stories so the minority takes it seriously
Answer A. The fact supports calm skill-building. The existence of serious cases is the reason to teach at all. Source: Academy Module 1, Calm Fact 1; self-check Q2
Which message is a well-formed skill message?
'Hackers are everywhere.'
'Everyone online is lying.'
'Never share anything online.'
'If an account asks for your password or code, hackles up: pause and check with a trusted adult.'
Answer D. A good skill message names a signal, one concrete action and a person to tell, in a hopeful, shame-free tone. Source: Academy Module 1, Activity 1.3; self-check Q10
An article says Thorn found that about 1 in 25 teens have had deepfake nudes created of them. What does the kit's check say?
The article is right; Thorn's figure is 1 in 25
Thorn reported 1 in 17 teens; '1 in 25' is the UNICEF figure for some countries, so the article's attribution is wrong
Thorn's figure is 1 in 8, which is the same thing
Neither organization has reported such a figure

Answer B. Round 1 corrected this exact error: 1 in 17 (Thorn, 1,200 US young people) and 1 in 8 who know someone targeted; 1 in 25 is UNICEF in some countries. Source: Fact-Check Report Round 1, items 4.8 to 4.10
Which sentence for a parent handout is the most defensible?
'Every statistic in this handout is guaranteed accurate.'
'Studies show Hackles prevents sextortion.'
'Research proves fear-based warnings backfire in online safety.'
'The evidence on fear appeals is mixed, and direct evidence for online safety is thin, so we teach calm skills with practice.'
Answer D. The kit says not to claim fear appeals are proven to backfire in this field and that no trial shows the program prevents harm. Source: Academy Module 1; Assessment Pack Section 13
In the kit's rule of thumb for a passphrase, what is the minimum?
One clever word with symbols
Five or more unrelated words, at least 15 characters in total, ideally chosen at random
A pet's name plus the year
Any eight characters changed monthly

Answer B. NIST SP 800-63B-4 sets 15 characters as the minimum for a password used alone. CISA suggests 5 to 7 words and 16 or more characters. Source: Academy Module 2, Part 1; Fact-Check Report Round 1, items 6.1 and 6.2
According to Module 2, which habit matters most?
Changing it every week
Sharing it with a trusted friend
A unique, long passphrase for each important account
Special characters in a short word
Answer C. Length beats cleverness, and reuse is the real enemy. Source: Academy Module 2, self-check Q1
Why is reusing a password the real problem?
When one site is hacked, stolen email and password lists are tried on other sites, so one leak can open every account that shares the key
Hackers cannot guess reused passwords
Websites cannot store reused passwords
Reuse makes a password shorter
Answer A. The Key Ring idea: one key for six doors means six open doors after a leak. Source: Academy Module 2, 'Why reuse is the problem'
What does Module 2 say about a login code a service sends you?
It is safe to share if the person sounds friendly
A moderator may need it to fix your account
A code is a key: nobody who is really helping you will ask you to read it to them
Support staff may ask for it to verify you
Answer C. Even a code from a text message can be tricked out of you. The rule holds for support, friends and moderators. Source: Academy Module 2, 2-step verification; self-check Q2
Why does Module 2 advise turning on 2-step verification for email first?
Email can reset many other accounts, so it is the master key
Email accounts do not have passwords
Email stores the most photos
Email is the only account that can be hacked
Answer A. Protect the account that can unlock the others. Source: Academy Module 2, 2-step verification rules; self-check Q3
What is a passkey?
A code texted to your phone
A password manager's master phrase
A cryptographic key on your device unlocked by fingerprint, face or screen lock, replacing a typed password
A longer password written on paper
Answer C. Nothing to type and nothing to hand over in a phishing message. Support varies by service, and recovery needs planning. Source: Academy Module 2, Passkeys; self-check Q6
Why can a passkey resist a phishing message?
It expires every hour
There is nothing to type or hand over, and the key only works for the real site on your device
It is stored in plain text where fake sites cannot see it
It is a very long password
Answer B. The kit's description: nothing to copy and nothing to reuse. NIST treats such authenticators as phishing resistant. Source: Academy Module 2, Passkeys; Fact-Check Report Round 1, item 6.5
Which invented passphrase best fits the kit's rule of thumb?
Tr0ub4dor&3
P@ssw0rd!
violet anchor pencil toast marble
Fluffy2012
Answer C. Five unrelated words, over 15 characters, silly and memorable. The others are short, common patterns or famous substitutions. Source: Academy Module 2, 'What makes a good password'
What does NIST SP 800-63B-4 say about forcing regular password changes, as summarized in the kit?
Passwords must be changed every 30 days
Verifiers must not require periodic changes without evidence of compromise
Changes are required only for children
Passwords must change after every login

Answer B. The kit cites the current revision (Aug 2025): no composition rules, no routine periodic changes, a blocklist check, and at least 64 characters allowed. Source: Academy Module 2, Part 1; Fact-Check Report Round 1, item 6.1
Which are the five hackles-raisers taught for phishing and scams?
Spelling, color, logo, font and length
Urgency, secrecy, too good to be true, the ask, and does not add up
Speed, price, brand, color and sound
Sender, subject, date, size and language
Answer B. None of the five depends on technology, so they travel across apps. Source: Academy Module 2, Part 2
A message says, 'Your account will be deleted in 1 hour. Click to confirm your password.' Which hackles-raisers are present?
Secrecy only
Urgency and the ask
None of them
Too good to be true only
Answer B. A deadline is urgency and a request to confirm a password is the ask. Pause and check another way. Source: Academy Module 2, self-check Q4
What is the Own-Door rule in the Facilitator Kit?
Reply to the sender and ask if it is real
Do not use the link, number or contact in the message; open the site or app yourself, call a number you already had, or ask in person
Click the link only if it looks professional
Forward the message to a friend to check
Answer B. Check another way, using a door you already trust. Source: Facilitator Kit Handout H4; Academy Module 2
A student tells you she typed her game password into a fake giveaway page. Which response fits the kit?
'Thank you for telling me. It is not your fault. Let's tell a trusted adult and use the official steps to secure the account.'
'Don't tell anyone; we will fix it quietly.'
'How could you be so careless?'
'Never play that game again.'
Answer A. Shame-free, tell an adult, official recovery. Blame makes the next disclosure less likely. Source: Academy Module 2, self-check Q10
Why does the kit say 'Never share personal information online' is not enough on its own?
It is a complete safety plan
It is illegal advice
It is vague and cannot be followed perfectly, so it should be paired with 'who is asking, why, and tell a trusted adult'
It applies only to adults
Answer C. The kit frames a better rule: who is asking, why, and do I trust them, plus telling. Source: Academy Module 2, 'A privacy rule that does not work'
What does the 3-2-1 backup rule say?
Three passwords, two locks, one code
Three copies, on two kinds of storage, with one stored elsewhere
Three devices, two accounts, one email
Three updates a year, two restarts, one backup
Answer B. The kit adds that backups should be tested, and for most teachers an approved cloud plus a second location is enough. Source: Academy Module 2, Part 5; Concepts Lab Demo 10
Why does Demo 10 stress restoring a backup at least once?
Backups only work if restored weekly
Restoring makes files smaller
Restoring deletes the backup
A tested copy kept elsewhere beats panic; a copy you have never restored is only a hope
Answer D. The big idea is another copy, somewhere else, that you know works. Source: Concepts Lab Demo 10
What is the 'mosaic effect' in Demo 9?
Small, harmless facts combine into a picture that points to one person
An image filter
A password made of tiles
A map of Wi-Fi coverage
Answer A. Alone one footprint rarely matters; together they form a profile. The demo uses a fictional person, Quinn. Source: Concepts Lab Demo 9
Which three families of proof does Demo 6 use for authentication?
A name, an address and a phone number
Something you type, click and send
Something you know, something you have, something you are
A username, a nickname and a code word
Answer C. A second proof from a different family stops most takeovers from a stolen password alone. Source: Concepts Lab Demo 6
What does Demo 7 teach about updates?
Updates make old holes larger
Updates only add new features
Updates are optional for security
An update is a fix for a known hole, and the race is between the fix reaching devices and someone misusing the hole
Answer D. Software has mistakes; some are holes. Every copy needs the fix. Source: Concepts Lab Demo 7; Academy Module 2 Part 4; self-check Q7
Why do well-built sites store a hash (a one-way fingerprint) of a password instead of the password?
It lets staff read passwords more easily
The site can check what you type without keeping it, and a stolen list of fingerprints is much less harmful than a stolen list of passwords
It makes login slower on purpose for every user
Hashes can be reversed instantly to show the password
Answer B. Demo 2's big idea is the one-way fingerprint. Salting and slow hashes are taught at the 9-12 level. Source: Concepts Lab Demo 2
The kit says 'at least 15 characters (CISA recommends 16 or more)'. Why are both numbers there?
Both numbers are guesses
15 is for children and 16 is for adults
The two agencies disagree and the kit picked one at random
NIST sets 15 as the minimum for a password used alone, while CISA recommends at least 16 characters or 5 to 7 unrelated words
Answer D. Round 1 corrected the earlier rule to reflect both sources. Source: Fact-Check Report Round 1, items 6.1 and 6.2
A slide says 'MFA blocks over 99 percent of attacks, says Microsoft.' How should it be handled?
Raise it to 100 percent for emphasis
Delete all mention of MFA
Present it as a proven national statistic
Label it as a vendor claim (99.9 percent of account compromise attacks, 2019, citing a SANS white paper), indicative not exact, and note CISA gives no percentage
Answer D. Round 1 corrected the wording and kept the caution. Source: Fact-Check Report Round 1, item 6.3; Concepts Lab Demo 6
A colleague wants to paste a student's name and a disclosure note into a chatbot to tidy the wording. What does the kit say?
Do not paste student names, work containing personal details or disclosure notes into a chatbot, and follow your district's AI policy [VERIFY]
It is fine if the chatbot is popular
It is fine if the name is shortened to initials
It is fine for notes, but not for names
Answer A. Module 3 sets this limit for teacher use of AI tools. Student data and disclosures stay out of chatbots. Source: Academy Module 3, 'A note on teacher use'
Which four patterns does Module 3 teach as showing up in every app?
Speed, Cost, Volume, Size
Pressure, Secrecy, The Ask, The Move
Name, Age, Place, School
Games, Chats, Video, Feeds
Answer B. Every risk in Module 1 is a variation on these four. Source: Academy Module 3, Part 2
Which pairing of pattern and response is correct?
Secrecy: Pause. The Ask: Tell. Pressure: Check.
The Move: Click. The Ask: Reply. Secrecy: Share.
Secrecy: Tell. The Ask: Check. Pressure: Pause.
Pressure: Tell. Secrecy: Check. The Ask: Pause.
Answer C. Pressure gets a Pause, secrecy gets a Tell, the ask gets a Check, and the move gets a Pause and a question about why the new place is more private. Source: Academy Module 3, Part 2 table
Which four adult reactions does Module 3 say make children stop telling?
Panic, punishment, lecture, minimizing
Delay, distraction, laughter and gifts
Phone calls, e-mails, texts and letters
Praise, thanks, questions and silence
Answer A. Each ends the conversation. Take them off the table in advance with the promise: you will not be in trouble for telling me things. Source: Academy Module 3, Part 3
A student says, 'My friend got a weird message. What should she do?' What is the best reply?
'Is it actually you?'
'That sounds stressful. I'm glad your friend has someone like you. Here is what I would suggest for her... and you can always tell me about anything too.'
'That is nothing to worry about.'
'Tell your friend to stop using that app.'
Answer B. Treat 'my friend' as real and keep the door open. Asking 'is it you?' can close it. Source: Academy Module 3, 'When my friend means me'
Which question is the best open question for a student about a game?
'Do you play every night?'
'Is that game safe?'
'What do you like about it, and what is annoying?'
'You are not talking to strangers, right?'
Answer C. Open questions invite explanation. Yes and no questions and loaded questions end conversations. Source: Academy Module 3, curiosity script; Module 5 Part 3
Which AI companion idea is part of the kit's 'fact sheet, not a scare'?
It forgets everything you type
It can agree too much, so it is not a substitute for a trusted adult
It is a person on the other end
It is always a reliable source of facts
Answer B. The kit lists: not a person, can be wrong, can agree too much, remembers and stores, not a substitute for a trusted adult. Source: Academy Module 3, World 3
What did Pew Research Center report in December 2025 about US teens and AI chatbots?
95 percent, about half daily
64 percent say they use AI chatbots, about 3 in 10 daily
99 percent, all daily
14 percent, about 1 in 100 daily
Answer B. [VERIFIED 2026-10-05 in the kit; 1,458 teens surveyed Sept 25 to Oct 9, 2025.] Source: Academy Module 3, World 3; Fact-Check Report Round 1, item 4.16
A speaker says 'one in three teens discuss serious matters with AI instead of a person.' What is wrong?
The statistic is correct as stated
Common Sense reported about one in three AI-companion users, not one in three of all teens
The true figure is one in three of all adults
Common Sense reported that nobody does this
Answer B. The denominator matters. Round 1 corrected the kit on this point. Source: Fact-Check Report Round 1, items 4.13 and 4.14
Why does Module 3 say 'a group chat is not a private room'?
Anything can be screenshotted, forwarded or shown to others
Group chats are always public websites
Group chats delete messages automatically
Only teachers can see group chats
Answer A. This is the key idea for children about group chats. Source: Academy Module 3, World 2
A chat goes quiet whenever one student posts. Which upstander moves does the kit's 6-8 'Group Chat Dynamics' lesson practice?
Screenshotting and posting the chat publicly
Waiting to see what happens
Joining in so you are not the next target
A quiet check-in, saying 'not cool' in the chat, leaving the chat, and telling a trusted adult
Answer D. These are the upstander moves named in Module 3. Source: Academy Module 3, World 2 (Hackles connection)
In Demo 12, what is the better habit than trying to spot a fake by its flaws?
Share it to see what others say
Trust any image that looks sharp
Decide it is fake because it is shocking
Verify the source: find the original, look for other reliable confirmation, and use a second channel for urgent requests
Answer D. Fakes improve, so verification habits outlast flaw-spotting. Source: Concepts Lab Demo 12
What is the 'liar's dividend' in Demo 12?
Wrongly dismissing real evidence as fake because fakes exist
A tax on synthetic media
The profit made by deepfake apps
A reward for exposing fakes
Answer A. Good defenders are careful, not cynical. Source: Concepts Lab Demo 12
A shocking photo of a public figure is spreading. What should a student do first, according to Demo 12 and the Assessment Pack?
Share it fast while it is trending
Check the original source and look for confirmation from reliable outlets before sharing
Decide it is real if it looks real
Decide it is fake because it is shocking
Answer B. Both gut reactions skip checking. The Assessment Pack 9-12 survey item uses this answer key. Source: Assessment Pack Section 6 item 7; Concepts Lab Demo 12
What does Module 3 say about the research on screens and well-being?
It sets a single daily limit for everyone
It proves screens cause harm in all children
It is mixed and still developing; quality, content, context, sleep and what screens replace seem to matter more than a number on a clock
It proves screens have no effect
Answer C. The kit points to the AAP's family media plan approach [VERIFIED 2026-10-05: healthychildren.org]. Source: Academy Module 3, Part 4
A teacher tells students that several state attorneys general have 'proved' a game company harms children. How should this be corrected?
These are allegations and fast-moving developments, not settled findings, so do not state them as fact in class [VERIFY current status]
Say the actions were all dismissed
Remove the topic entirely and never discuss games
Add that the companies have admitted guilt
Answer A. Module 3 and the evidence file label them allegations. Source: Academy Module 3, World 1; Evidence file Section 2.6
In Week 4's Curiosity Interview, which behavior fits the five-step script?
Correcting the partner's app choices
Listening about 70 percent of the time and reflecting back what you heard without judging
Writing down names and details to keep
Offering a lecture on risks
Answer B. Be curious, listen more than you talk, reflect back, ask open questions, offer do not impose. Source: Academy Module 3, Part 3
What is Rule 1 of the five rules of safety teaching that works?
Skills over information
Information over skills
Fear over calm
Assemblies over lessons
Answer A. Good lessons teach a few facts and one concrete skill to practice. Source: Academy Module 4, Part 1
Which is a skill-based objective (the 'Teacher test')?
After this, students will appreciate security
After this, students will know that passwords are important
After this, students will be aware of hackers
After this, students can say 'No, I'll check with my grown-up' when someone asks for a password
Answer D. A skill is a verb students can show. Know, be aware and appreciate cannot be observed. Source: Academy Module 4, Rule 1
Why does role-play work for safety skills?
It tests children on facts
It replaces the need to tell an adult
It scares children into compliance
It makes the words available when the real moment comes; a child who has practiced 'I need help' can say it once in a hard moment
Answer D. Practice builds a reflex. Source: Academy Module 4, Rule 2
Which role-play practice does Module 4 recommend?
Assign the most shy student to play the victim
Ask students to act out graphic details
Let students play the helper, not the victim, and have the adult play the difficult person with a clear signal for stepping out of character
Use real stories from students
Answer C. Also use puppets or character cards for younger children so no child plays the 'bad guy.' Source: Academy Module 4, Rule 2
Which framing replaces a fear message with a tool?
'If you talk to a stranger, something terrible could happen.'
'If anyone asks for secrets or pictures, your hackles go up. Pause and tell.'
'Your life will be ruined.'
'You will be hacked!'
Answer B. The Hackles framing gives a signal and an action. Source: Academy Module 4, Rule 3 table
Which three promises does Hackles language make?
Nobody will ever know; nothing will happen; everything is private
You will always be right; you can never be fooled; you must never share
Every answer will be graded; every mistake is recorded; every parent is told
A false alarm is fine and welcome; it is never your fault; you will not be in trouble for telling
Answer D. Say them aloud often, especially to older students, who assume the opposite. Source: Academy Module 4, Rule 4
Which phrase best replaces 'Why did you click it?'
'You should have known better.'
'Good kids do not do that.'
'What happened next?'
'How could you?'
Answer C. 'Why' questions can sound like blame. Source: Academy Module 4, Rule 4 table
Why does the kit say 'never' language invites failure?
Adults should say 'always' instead
Children inevitably share some things, so 'never share your name' sets them up to feel they failed; 'think first' and 'check first' are more honest
Children are not capable of safe behavior
'Never' is too gentle for safety lessons
Answer B. Prefer 'think first,' 'ask a trusted adult,' 'check first.' Source: Academy Module 4, Rule 4
What is a spiral curriculum, as used in Hackles?
Repeating the identical lesson every year
Each grade band returns to the same core routine and strands at a more advanced level
Teaching only the newest apps
Teaching all topics in one long unit
Answer B. One lesson does not do it; revisit a little deeper over months and years. Source: Academy Module 4, Rule 5
Two grade 4 password lessons are compared. Which is the good lesson?
The teacher reads ten password rules from slides and gives a quiz
The teacher warns that bad passwords will cost students everything
The teacher assigns a chapter on password history
Groups build the funniest four-word passphrase, then use a crack-timer card; exit ticket asks for a new rule and when to tell a grown-up
Answer D. The good lesson has students create, compare, discuss and decide in a calm tone. Source: Academy Module 4, Part 2, Pair 1

Two grade 8 lessons on pressure online: A shows graphic stories of what happens to children who share pictures; B uses calm case files about a fictional character and rehearses STOP, SAVE, TELL, REPORT. Which statement is correct?
A is better because it motivates through fear
B follows the evidence-informed approach: no graphic detail, a skill, and help-seeking, while A risks shame, fear and silence
A is better because it is more realistic
Both are equally good
Answer B. The kit's Good versus Weak pair says exactly this. Source: Academy Module 4, Part 2, Pair 3
Which item is on the 'good lesson' checklist?
Gives students a role other than victim
Includes a graphic example for realism
Requires every student to share a personal story
Runs 45 minutes
Answer A. Also: one clear skill, a rehearsal, no fear or shame, ends with who to tell, about 15 minutes, a check, a safe way to disclose. Source: Academy Module 4, 'The good lesson checklist'
What caution does Module 4 give about gamification?
Use games that practice the skill, never games that act out the harm
Never use games
Games should be graded
Use points to rank children against each other
Answer A. Fun matters, and the game must teach the skill. Source: Academy Module 4, Part 4
A colleague says, 'Can't we just show a video? Fear gets attention.' What is the best reply?
A video alone is information; add a short rehearsal and a calm tone, because fear without a skill is just fear and shame blocks telling
Say a video is the same as an active lesson
Agree, because attention is the main goal
Say videos are always banned
Answer A. The kit's rules favor rehearsal and calm skill practice. A video can serve as a hook only. Source: Academy Module 4, Scenario 4.A and Rules 1 to 3
A student who 'already knows it all' keeps interrupting. What does the kit suggest?
Quiz them in front of the class
Send them out of the room
Ignore them for the rest of the term
Give them a role, such as a helper, detective or demonstrator
Answer D. Module 5's management table says to give know-it-alls and jokers a role. Source: Academy Module 4, Scenario 4.B; Module 5 Part 4
During a role-play, several students giggle. Which response fits?
Cancel the lesson
Name it kindly ('A lot of us laugh when things feel awkward') and keep going
Single out one student
Stop and punish the class
Answer B. Giggling is often nervous energy, not disrespect. Source: Academy Module 4, Scenario 4.C; Module 5 Part 4
In the student plan STOP, SAVE, TELL, REPORT, what does SAVE mean?
Save and share any image as proof
Save the password to a document
Delete everything to be safe
Keep the account name, links, dates and text threats; never save or share images
Answer D. SAVE means text evidence only. Source: Academy Module 4, Rule 1; Module 6 Part 4
Why does Module 4 prefer 'someone who is pressuring you' to 'predator' and 'the person it happened to' to 'victim' when talking with children?
The words are too long
The words are more frightening
Shame-free, concrete language is easier for children to act on and keeps telling safe
The words are legally prohibited in classrooms
Answer C. The language table lists 'predator' and 'victim' (to a child) as phrases to avoid. Source: Academy Module 4, Rule 4 table
What are the four parts of a 15-minute Hackles lesson and their times?
Hook 2, Activity 8, Discuss 3, Takeaway 2
Lecture 10, Quiz 3, Homework 1, Test 1
Hook 5, Activity 5, Discuss 3, Takeaway 2
Video 5, Video 5, Video 3, Video 2
Answer A. The same skeleton is used in every Teacher Guide. Source: Academy Module 5, Part 1
What does 'one skill, one phrase, one gesture' mean?
One teacher, one student, one device
Three separate lessons in one
One fact, one date, one quiz
A lesson should be summarized by a single skill, a repeatable sentence and a hand signal; more means it is probably two lessons
Answer D. Examples: Pause before you click; 'Hackles up? Pause, Check, Tell'; Pause Palm. Source: Academy Module 5, Part 1
Why must the Hook stay at about two minutes?
If you are still talking at minute three, you have lost the class, and the activity is where students learn
Hooks are not allowed to be fun
The Takeaway needs 8 minutes
Students cannot listen for more than a minute
Answer A. Hook rules: do not scare, do not exceed two minutes, say what you will practice. Source: Academy Module 5, The Hook
Which order lists the question ladder from lower to higher level?
Apply, recall, evaluate, create, explain
Explain, recall, create, apply, evaluate
Recall, explain, apply, evaluate, create
Create, evaluate, apply, explain, recall
Answer C. Start with what did we notice and climb toward how could we improve it. Source: Academy Module 5, Part 3
Which question is open rather than closed?
'Is that right?'
'Was that a scam?'
'What made you think it was a scam?'
'Did you tell an adult?'
Answer C. Open questions invite explanation. Source: Academy Module 5, Part 3
A student says, 'I would just send it.' What is the best response?
Ignore the comment
'That is a terrible idea.'
Ask the student to explain in front of everyone why they are careless
'Thanks for being honest. Lots of people feel that pressure. Let's practice a different response,' then follow up privately
Answer D. A worrying answer is information, not a reason to shame. Source: Academy Module 5, Part 3 (Responding to answers)
How long should wait time be after asking a question?
30 seconds
Under one second
About 3 to 5 seconds
Two minutes
Answer C. Wait time raises quality and participation. Source: Academy Module 5, Part 2
What is the purpose of the pass card?
It preserves safety and dignity: any student may say 'pass' without explaining
It lets students skip lessons
It excuses students from homework
It records who is uncomfortable
Answer A. Always available, especially in sensitive lessons. Source: Academy Module 5, Part 2
You are 12 minutes in and the activity is not finished. What does the time rescue table say?
Add a second activity
Skip the takeaway
Extend the lesson by 10 minutes
Cut one round of practice; keep the takeaway and the open door
Answer D. Never cut the takeaway and the open door. Source: Academy Module 5, Part 4 (Time rescue)
Which is one of the 'four mistakes to avoid above all'?
Giving students a role
Promising secrecy
Starting with a hook
Using a hand signal
Answer B. The four: making a child the example, promising secrecy, ignoring the open door, teaching without prep for disclosures. Source: Academy Module 5, Part 6
A student starts a long personal story in front of the class. What do you do?
Let the story continue so everyone learns
Tell them to stop and not speak again
Ask follow-up questions in front of the class
Thank them, redirect gently ('let's keep the details between us and talk privately after'), and follow up that day
Answer D. This protects the student's privacy and keeps a path open for disclosure. Source: Academy Module 5, Part 4
What is the Takeaway formula?
Fact plus quiz plus score
Story plus joke plus video
Skill plus gesture plus promise
Warning plus consequence plus rule
Answer C. Example: Pause before you click (Pause Palm), plus 'a false alarm is fine and it is never your fault.' Source: Academy Module 5, The Takeaway
In the Micro-Teach Rubric, which total marks Hackles-Ready practice?
6 to 11
18 to 24 out of 24
Only 24
Answer C. Six rows scored 1 to 4: 6 to 11 keep practicing; 12 to 17 solid; 18 to 24 Hackles-Ready. Source: Academy Module 5, Part 7
Only five students are active during the 8-minute activity. Which rubric row and design rule does this violate?
Active practice: every student should do the skill at least twice, so redesign the activity
Skill focus: the skill is unnamed
Safety and closure: the close was calm
Tone and language: no shaming occurred
Answer A. The activity design rule is that everyone does something. Source: Academy Module 5, The Activity; rubric row 3
A student's exit ticket says, 'Something happened on my account and I don't want to say.' What is the right step?
Read exit tickets the same day, treat it as a possible disclosure, follow the First 10 Minutes and your policy, and involve the counselor
Contact the family first without checking policy
Post the note on the board to ask who wrote it
Wait until the end of term to read the exit tickets
Answer A. Module 5 says to check exit tickets for worrying content on the same day. Source: Academy Module 5, Scenario 5.B and Part 4
What is the 'I do, we do, you do' pattern?
Students teach, teacher watches, parents grade
Teacher models, the class tries together, then pairs or groups practice twice
Teacher talks, class listens, class takes a test
Teacher reads, students copy, students sign
Answer B. Typical timing: 1 minute I do, 2 minutes we do, 5 minutes you do. Source: Academy Module 5, The Activity
Which hook follows Module 5's hook rules?
A three-minute statistics lecture
'Imagine something terrible happens to you online.'
Hold up a fake pop-up card and ask for a thumbs up or down: 'Detectives, is this real?'
A graphic news story about a victim
Answer C. A good hook is curious, calm, short and names the skill. It never scares. Source: Academy Module 5, The Hook
The Peer Coaching Guide says not to add up Fun, Safe, Skill-based ratings or compare teachers. Why?
Because the ratings are always wrong
Because totals are required by law
Because teachers should never be observed
A rating is a conversation starter, not a grade; patterns matter more than single items, and only one grow is given
Answer D. The guide says to pick one grow and avoid comparing teachers. Source: Peer Coaching Guide Section 3
Which three sentences does the kit teach for the first moments of a disclosure?
'I won't tell anyone. It will be fine. Forget it.'
'Are you sure? That is odd. Delete it.'
'Thank you for telling me. This is not your fault. You are not in trouble.'
'Why did you do that? Who else knows? Show me.'
Answer C. The three sentences reassure without blame. Source: Academy Module 6, Part 3; Disclosure Guide Section 2
What is the teacher's role in a disclosure?
Counselor who treats the child
Detective who confronts the other person
Recognition and response: listen, reassure, protect evidence safely, report, hand off, document, and look after the child and yourself
Investigator who finds out what happened
Answer C. You are not an investigator, a therapist or a police officer. Source: Disclosure Guide Section 1
Why should you not promise a child 'I won't tell anyone'?
Because teachers are not allowed to speak to children privately
Because children do not care about secrecy
Because secrets are always safe to keep
You may be required to tell people whose job is to help, and breaking a promise hurts more; say 'I can't keep this a secret, because I want to get you help. I will tell you who I tell.'
Answer D. Honesty about limits builds trust. Source: Academy Module 6, Part 3 Step 4; Script D
A second grader says, 'Somebody on my tablet game said not to tell my mom. He gives me gems.' What is the best response?
'Show me the chat.'
'He is probably just a kind player.'
'Thank you for telling me. You are not in trouble. Can you tell me a little more?' Then report on reasonable suspicion without asking for names or details
Phone the child's mother before anyone else
Answer C. Secrecy and gifts from an unknown person are a reasonable-suspicion pattern. Do not interrogate, and do not contact the family first. Source: Academy Module 6, Script A and debrief
What is the typical standard that triggers a report, as described in the kit?
A police report
A confession
Reasonable suspicion or reason to believe, not proof; the exact standard varies by state [VERIFY]
Proof beyond doubt
Answer C. Reporters do not have to prove abuse occurred. Source: Academy Module 6, Part 2; Fact-Check Report Round 1, item 3.3
Why does the kit say that telling your principal may not satisfy your own duty?
The duty is identical in every state
Principals are never involved in reporting
Teachers are never legally required to report
In many states the duty is personal and internal reporting may not relieve it, while procedures vary by state; check your state and district policy [VERIFY]

Answer D. Round 1 corrected 'most states' to 'many states.' The practical message is to report yourself and also tell the administrator per policy. Source: Fact-Check Report Round 1, item 3.4; Academy Module 6 Part 2
What must you never do with suspected sexual images of a minor?
Keep them to show to the principal
Forward them to the counselor
View, copy, download, forward, print or screenshot them
Print one copy for the file

Answer C. Under federal law, knowing possession or sharing is a serious crime with narrow defenses; secure the device per policy [counsel to confirm]. Source: Academy Module 6, Step 5; Disclosure Guide Step 5
A student says a classmate has an intimate image on a phone. A colleague suggests you 'just look to check.' What do you do?
Delete the image to protect the classmate
Look briefly to confirm
Ask another student to forward it to you
Do not look; ask the student not to delete or forward anything; secure the device per policy; report personally and promptly
Answer D. Good intentions are not a safe assumption. Authorities collect evidence lawfully. Source: Academy FAQ 16; Disclosure Guide Step 5
In STOP, SAVE, TELL, REPORT, what is saved?
The password to the account
Nothing; everything is deleted
Account names, profile links, dates and threatening text, never images
Copies of any image sent
Answer C. SAVE means text evidence. Source: Academy Module 6, Part 4; Assessment Pack Section 6
What does NCMEC's Take It Down service do, according to the kit?
Reports the child to the school
Removes any adult image from any site instantly
Deletes a child's account
Helps remove images of people who were under 18 when the image was made from participating platforms, using a hash so the image is never uploaded. It does not work on encrypted platforms
Answer D. People 18 or older are directed to StopNCII.org. [VERIFIED 2026-10-05: takeitdown.ncmec.org] Source: Fact-Check Report Round 1, items 1.2 and 1.6; Academy Module 6
Which entry belongs in your documentation of a disclosure?
Your guess about what really happened
An opinion about the family
A diagnosis
The child's exact words in quotation marks, date, time, place, who you told and what you did
Answer D. Document facts only. Source: Academy Module 6, Step 7
Where should a private conversation with a child take place?
In a car
Alone in a closed room
A private place that is still visible to other adults, with the door open or a glass window; never alone behind a closed door
In front of the class
Answer C. This protects the child and the adult. Source: Academy Module 6, Step 1
A student blurts out in class, 'That happened to me!' about a threat and a picture. What is the best immediate response?
Ignore it until the lesson ends tomorrow
Ask them for details in front of the class
Let classmates ask questions
Thank them, say you will talk privately in a moment, calm the class and arrange for another adult to supervise, then meet the student that day
Answer D. Contain the moment without shaming, protect privacy, and move to the First 10 Minutes. Source: Academy Module 6, Script C and 'Disclosures in front of the class'
After a lesson on pressure online, a student says, 'It's kind of me.' after speaking of 'a friend.' What now?
'Why did you not say so?'
Promise to tell nobody
Thank them calmly, say the three sentences, be honest about telling people who can help, and do not ask to see messages or images
'I knew it was you.'
Answer C. Accept the shift calmly. Honest limits and no pressure. Source: Academy Module 6, Script B
A student asks, 'Promise you won't tell?' Which reply is best?
'Only if it is minor.'
'I promise.'
'I want to hear it. If it is about someone being hurt or in danger, I must get help from others. I will tell you who and why, and I will not go behind your back.'
'I can't promise anything and I do not want to hear it.'
Answer C. It is honest and kind and leaves the door open; promising secrecy and then breaking it harms trust. Source: Academy Module 6, Script D
Which crisis resources does the kit list for young people and adults?
A school email alias
211 and 311 only
988 (call or text), Crisis Text Line (text HOME to 741741), and NCMEC CyberTipline (1-800-843-5678; report.cybertip.org)
The police non-emergency line only
Answer C. [VERIFIED 2026-10-05: 988lifeline.org, crisistextline.org, report.cybertip.org]. Call 911 for immediate danger. Source: Fact-Check Report Round 1, items 1.1, 1.3, 1.4
A parent phones and says, 'My daughter told me she told you something. What did she say?' What is the best response?
Say you cannot talk to parents at all
Repeat what the daughter said
Stay warm and share no details, connect them to the counselor, tell your administrator, and consider whether a family member could be involved before sharing anything
Tell the parent to ask a friend
Answer C. Follow policy and involve the counselor. Source: Academy Module 6, Script E
What is secondary traumatic stress, in plain language?
Hearing about a child's hard experience can affect you even though you were not there; it is common and does not mean you did something wrong [VERIFY with a mental health source if cited]
A form of blame
A sign that you should not teach any topic
A condition only counselors get
Answer A. Care plan layers: right after, same day, that evening, that week, longer term. Source: Academy Module 6, Part 6
Which statement is a phrase to avoid in a disclosure, and why?
'I believe you.' It is too short
'Your parents will be so upset.' It adds fear
'Thank you for telling me.' It is a form of praise
'What would help you feel safest?' It is leading
Answer B. The avoid list also includes why questions, shock, 'I won't tell anyone,' 'I'm sure it's fine,' 'Let me see,' and 'Are you sure?' Source: Academy Module 6, Part 4
For a cyberbullying incident without sexual content or a threat, which steps does the Disclosure Guide list?

Support the child targeted, help them save text evidence, document, report within bullying policy, avoid face-to-face mediation, support the child who was unkind, and check in at a day, a week and a month
Put both children together immediately to settle it
Post the incident in a staff chat
Delete all messages
Answer A. Do not mediate in a way that re-harms. Source: Disclosure Guide Section 5
Which of these needs immediate escalation to an administrator and counselor?
A game score argument
A late assignment
A mean nickname used once
Threats of violence, self-harm statements, sexual content, doxxing, or a child saying they feel unsafe at school or home
Answer D. These are the red flags listed in the bullying section. Source: Disclosure Guide Section 5
You are not sure whether a student's comment is reportable. What does the kit advise?
Wait a week to see if more details appear
Ask the student's friends
Question the student until sure
Report if you are unsure, because the standard is suspicion not certainty; ask your administrator or the CPS hotline but do not delay while waiting
Answer D. The threshold is reasonable suspicion, not proof. Source: Academy Module 6, Scenario 6.C and Part 2
When should you not contact the family first?
Never; always call the family first
Only if the child is over 12
Whenever a child is upset
If a family member could be involved, the child asks you not to out of fear for their safety, or authorities advise otherwise
Answer D. Follow district policy and CPS or law enforcement guidance. Source: Disclosure Guide Step 6; Academy Module 6 Step 6
Which are the five principles for every lesson in Module 7?
Many ways in; no one is singled out; everyone has someone; assume good intentions in families; safety first, always
One way in; call on volunteers; public sharing; family contact; lecture
Speed; volume; testing; ranking; grading
Fear; rules; secrecy; penalty; reward
Answer A. Inclusion never lowers safeguards. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 1
A child needs to disclose, and a classmate offers to translate. What do you do?
Ask the child to write in English
Do not use a classmate or sibling; offer a drawing or note in any language, a trusted bilingual adult or an interpreter service
Accept the classmate as interpreter
Delay the conversation
Answer B. Children should not interpret for sensitive conversations. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 2
Why does the kit say a bilingual buddy should be a choice and rotate?
So no child becomes the permanent translator or is put on the spot
Because translation is illegal
Because buddies are never helpful
Because it gives extra points
Answer A. Pairing is a support, not an obligation. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 2
A newcomer to the class cannot read an English poster about 'hackles.' What helps?
Ask the student to sit out
Pictures, gestures and the four hand signals, pre-taught key words, and teaching 'I need help' in home languages, verified by a fluent speaker [VERIFY]
Simplify by removing all safety content
Assign a longer text
Answer B. Hand signals do not depend on English. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 2; Scenario 7.A
What does Module 7 say about low-internet and no-device homes?
Exclude those students from the lesson
Assign online homework anyway
Treat low-device homes as a problem to fix
Do practice in class, never assign tasks needing a device at home, and remember low-device does not mean low-risk
Answer D. The kit is unplugged by default. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 5
Which are the six trauma-informed practices in Module 7?
Predictability, choice, safety, calm closings, warmth and respect, collaboration
Fear, secrecy, humor, argument, debate, volume
Testing, grading, sorting, ranking, shaming, timing
Speed, surprise, rank, reward, penalty, silence
Answer A. Reactions that look like misbehavior may be coping. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 4b
Which phrase helps in a trauma-informed classroom?
'Everyone else can do it.'
'Just get over it.'
'Stop being dramatic.'
'You have choices. Take the time you need. It is okay to pass.'
Answer D. The harmful list includes 'You are fine' and 'Why do you always...'. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 4b
A student laughs and withdraws during a heavy topic. What does the kit suggest?
Ignore all behavior
It may be coping; respond with calm and curiosity, then check in privately
Discipline immediately
Call the family at once
Answer B. Reactions that look like misbehavior may be a child coping with a heavy topic. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 4b 'Remember'
What does L.E.A.R.N. stand for?
Look, Explain, Argue, Reply, Notify
Leave, End, Avoid, Refuse, Never
Listen, Empathize, Agree where you can, Respond with facts and options, Next step
Learn, Educate, Assess, Review, Navigate
Answer C. A five-step response to parent pushback. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 7
A parent says, 'You are putting ideas in their heads.' Which reply fits?
'That is a thoughtful worry. The lessons avoid graphic detail and give children tools; they usually meet these things online already' [VERIFY any research cited]
'Our principal decided; I cannot discuss it.'
'You are wrong, and the statistics prove it.'
'Your child will be fine, so do not worry.'
Answer A. Respond with facts and options, not an argument. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 7 table
A parent asks, 'Why are you collecting data on my child?' What is the accurate answer for a class using Hackles?
'Hackles itself collects no student accounts or data. Any tally I keep is class-level and follows district policy.'
'We cannot tell you.'
'The company stores names for ten years.'
'We collect everything for research.'
Answer A. Hackles collects no student accounts and no student data; teachers keep paper, local, short-lived tallies per district policy [VERIFY]. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 7; Module 8 Part 1
A family member could be involved in a child's disclosure. Which message to the family is appropriate?
A message copying the child's words
None until you have followed the Disclosure Guide and your policy; do not use a routine concern message
A call to the family before reporting
A warm routine message describing the concern
Answer B. Sharing news of a concern applies to small, non-urgent matters only. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 6
What is the counselor's role in Parent Night?
To grade parents
To speak about what to do when a child tells you something hard and to help families pick a code word
To avoid answering questions
To take attendance
Answer B. In the 30-minute script the counselor voice leads 'When your child tells you something hard.' Source: Parent Night Presentation Script, Section 6
A family wants to opt a child out of a higher-care lesson. What is the kit's approach?
Thank them; families can opt a child out of specific lessons, and the counselor explains the process and the alternative activity
Make the child do the lesson online
Tell the child's peers
Refuse and require attendance
Answer A. Respect the family and keep the child included in a safe alternative. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 7; Principal Checklist Section 7
An angry parent raises their voice during a meeting about the lessons. What should you do?
Match their volume
Stay calm, set a boundary ('I want to help, and I will continue this when we can talk calmly'), end the conversation, and tell your administrator
Promise to cancel the lessons
Argue the statistics
Answer B. You do not need to absorb abuse. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 7 'When it escalates'
What does 'everyone has someone' mean in practice?
Every child must name a parent
Every child must have a phone
Make sure every child can name a safe adult, and that school helpers count
Every adult must be a counselor
Answer C. Some children have no safe adult at home, so school helpers matter. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 1
In the Inclusion Audit, which step in a lesson plan should be flagged?
A step with a pass card
A step that uses a hand signal
A step with pictures
A step that assumes a device, a quiet home, fluent English, fine-motor skills or a grown-up at home
Answer D. Circle it and write one alternative. Source: Academy Module 7, Try This Now and Activity 7.1
Which family message best matches the kit?
'This will protect your child from online harm.'
'We teach children skills, not fear. Your child will never be in trouble for telling. Lessons avoid graphic detail and collect no student accounts or data.'
'Your child is at serious risk.'
'The state requires this, so there is no choice.'
Answer B. Three simple messages from Module 7. Avoid promises of prevention and avoid fear. Source: Academy Module 7, Part 6
What are Module 8's three questions to ask about teaching?
Is it graded? Is it published? Is it paid?
Did they learn? Would they act? Is it safe to tell?
Was it fun? Was it long? Was it cheap?
Who won? Who lost? Who left?
Answer B. The third is the most important and hardest to measure. Source: Academy Module 8, Part 1
What is the Tell-Readiness indicator?
The share of students who give the best answer on the two or three core 'would you tell' items
The number of disclosures a teacher receives
The grade on the final exam
The number of students in class
Answer A. It is the Assessment Pack's most meaningful number. Report it as a change in survey answers. Source: Academy Module 8, Part 2; Assessment Pack Section 7
Pre: 11 of 24 chose the best answer. Post: 17 of 22. What is the change in percentage points, rounded?
About +31 points (46 percent to 77 percent)
About +17 points
About +55 points
About +6 points
Answer A. 11/24 is about 46 percent and 17/22 is about 77 percent. The kit's honest summary adds that class sizes differed slightly. Source: Academy Module 8, Part 3 worked example
Core items pre: 26 of 72; post: 51 of 72. What is the Tell-Readiness change?
From 36 percent to 71 percent, +35 percentage points
+71 points
+51 points
+25 points
Answer A. 26/72 is about 36 percent and 51/72 is about 71 percent. Source: Assessment Pack Section 14, Step 3
Why may disclosures go up after lessons, according to the Assessment Pack?
Because the lessons cause more harm
Students feel safer to tell, which can be a sign the program is working; more or fewer disclosures does not map neatly to more or less harm
Because the survey is faulty
Because teachers invent them
Answer B. Do not treat an increase in disclosures as a failure. Source: Assessment Pack Section 13
Why does the kit say that with 24 students small changes may be noise?
One child is about 4 percentage points, so small shifts can come from a few students or chance
Surveys are never accurate
Percentages cannot be computed for 24
Statistics require 100 students
Answer A. Treat results as signals, not proof. Source: Academy Module 8, Part 3 reasonableness check
Which is the most honest claim for a report?
'Research proves this works.'
'More of my students said they would tell a trusted adult after the lessons (n = 24 matched pairs; no comparison group).'
'My lessons prevented abuse.'
'Our students are now safe from phishing.'
Answer B. Report changes in survey answers, the number of students, and the lack of a comparison group. Source: Academy Module 8, Honest claims; Assessment Pack Section 14 Step 8
What can a pre/post survey without a comparison group not show?
Cause, real-world behavior, honest answers under pressure, long-term effects
How many students are in class
Which items were skipped
Whether the survey printed
Answer A. Changes may reflect maturation, other lessons, news, repeated testing or chance. Source: Assessment Pack Section 13
How small a subgroup should you avoid reporting, per the kit?
Fewer than 1,000
Fewer than 100
Any subgroup of any size
Fewer than about ten students, subject to your district's suppression rule [VERIFY]
Answer D. Small groups may identify individuals. Source: Academy Module 8, Part 1; Assessment Pack Step 9
Matched pairs: 15 up, 7 same, 2 down among 24. Which statement fits the kit's example?
'Everyone improved.'
'Two students are failing.'
'Most students (15 of 24) improved. A few (2) went down. We look at those who did not move and offer more practice.'
'The program caused improvement in 15 students.'
Answer C. Report counts and offer additional practice. Source: Assessment Pack Section 14, Step 4
What are the four pieces of the Academy capstone?
Exam; essay; poster; video
Lesson Plan and Micro-Teach Evidence; Response Readiness Pack; Inclusion and Family Pack; Action Plan and Reflection
Quiz; survey; ticket; tally
Letter; chart; form; slide
Answer B. Together they provide evidence for all six competencies. Source: Academy Module 8, Part 7
What does the Academy require for Hackles-Ready on the capstone rubric?
Any three rows at 2
Row A only
At least five of six rows at 3 or above, no row at 1, and Row E (Respond) at 3 or above
All rows at 4
Answer C. Row E must be at least Hackles-Ready because response readiness is the most important competency for child safety. Source: Academy_Assessments, Section 6
Scores on the post survey went down. What does Scenario 8.A suggest?
Hide the results
Blame the students
Drop the program
Look at the answers before panicking; students may be more honest after learning, or the post survey may be harder; ask students safely what would make telling easier
Answer D. A drop can occur by chance and is worth examining only if it appears across several classes. Source: Academy Module 8, Scenario 8.A; Assessment Pack Step 6
A principal says, 'Our measures say we are great, so we are done.' What is the best reply?
Thank them, note the limits of surveys (no comparison group, self-report), and continue with glow-and-grow, delayed post surveys and observation
Say all measures are useless
Publish a claim of effectiveness
Agree and stop measuring

Answer A. Measures are signals for improvement. The Assessment Pack lists optional improvements such as a delayed post and a comparison group. Source: Academy Module 8, Scenario 8.B; Assessment Pack Step 7
What is the purpose of the teach-back?
To record the presenter
To check understanding and spread learning: you explain in your own words and the listener asks questions
To test the listener for mistakes
To grade the instructor
Answer B. It works for children, colleagues and families. Source: Academy Module 8, Part 5
A teacher plans to add a survey item asking students whether they have ever been bullied online. What does the kit say?
It is fine if no names are used
It is fine if anonymous

Keep student surveys to knowledge, skills and confidence; items about a student's own experiences can fall under PPRA protected areas and need counsel, parental review and consent [COUNSEL TO CONFIRM]
It is fine if the teacher gives it in class

Answer C. The kit warns that a survey on protected areas given by a school official is treated as required and needs written parental consent; an opt-out is not enough [VERIFIED 2026-10-05; re-verify]. Source: Assessment Pack, opening note and Section 6B
